jobs.title: SVP, Product
jobs.description:
About Toptal
Toptal is a global network of top talent in business, design, and technology that enables companies to scale their teams, on-demand. With $200+ million in annual revenue and team members based around the globe, Toptal is the world’s largest fully remote workforce.
We take the best elements of virtual teams and combine them with a support structure that encourages innovation, social interaction, and fun. We see no borders, move at a fast pace, and are never afraid to break the mold.
Position Description:
As SVP, Product, you will shape the vision as to where Toptal’s products and platforms go next and then drive the execution to build them. This is the most senior product role in the company. You will report to the Chief Executive Officer, sit on the executive team, and work collaboratively with our Engineering, Design, Finance, Marketing, New Businesses, Professional Services, and Customer leaders. AI is not a line item on your roadmap. It is the roadmap.
You should be Toptal’s foremost expert on what AI means for products and platforms. That means real depth in fine-tuning and post-training, agent design and evaluation, and the economics of running models in production, along with the judgment to know which applies to us. Work directly with our AI researchers rather than through them. We expect both the AI agenda and the product strategy to originate with you. We will react to your plan rather than hand you ours.
This is a hands-on role. You will write your own specs and pull your own data. When you think an agent could take over a piece of work, you will build a rough version and find out whether it holds up before anyone budgets for it. You will sit in product reviews and say what you actually think. We move fast, and we need Product setting the pace. You will own and set the standards for the hiring bar for the product team, bringing in talent that will advance Toptal to the next level.
Your remit runs across the business: the core platform, the talent and client experiences, the internal systems that run it, the products we take to market, and the data and AI platform underneath them. You will work hand in hand with Engineering on the platform all of it runs on, fold acquisitions and new products into the portfolio, and know growth marketing cold, because how a product reaches the market is part of building it.
Product is yours to shape at blazing speed: scoping, sizing the teams, planning headcount, and defining the role and the bar for every seat. None of that is beneath the role, and we are not interested in someone who thinks these tasks can be done properly by handing them off to HR. Hiring is the highest-leverage work you do, and we want someone who is visibly excited about landing an A player and treats an open seat as urgent. Your own dedication and hard work will set the tone, and the people you bring in should be inspired to do the best work of their careers on this team. We are looking for the person who will define what an AI-native product organization looks like and then run it successfully.
This is a remote position. Resumes and communication must be submitted in English.
Responsibilities:
The following information is intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed. It is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or required skills.
AI and agentic product
Own Toptal’s AI product strategy: where agents and models belong across the marketplace, the talent and client experiences, our internal systems, and the products we take to market, along with the business outcomes they carry.
Decide what we build with AI and what we do not, including build-versus-buy on models and tooling and the packaging and pricing of AI-enabled products.
Make AI quality measurable through evals, acceptance bars, and review loops, and partner with Engineering on the platform as its most demanding customer.
Rebuild how Product works using AI, raising the output and judgment of every product manager through AI-assisted discovery, research, prototyping, and analysis. Product managers have to want this rather than comply with it, and creating that pull is on you.
Portfolio and operating model
Own the vision, strategy, and multi-year roadmap for the whole portfolio: what we build, what we sunset, and how investment is distributed across growth, platform, and operational leverage.
Establish the product operating model and the metrics behind it, so decisions are made on evidence and user research rather than opinion.
Own the product integration of acquisitions and new products, and act as a senior voice of the customer for both talent and clients.
Team and accountability
Decide what a product team should look like now that the roles have blurred, where the product manager believes they can design and code, the engineer believes they can do product and design, and the designer believes they can code and do product.
Own resourcing and workforce planning, and hit time-sensitive hiring commitments.
Review the product work directly, develop people against a clear bar, and raise it as the organization grows.
In the first week, expect to:
Work to get up to speed with how the organization runs, including how our operational frameworks work.
Begin building relationships with the CEO, the executive team, and your direct reports.
Begin learning Toptal’s platform architecture, marketplace dynamics, internal tooling, and current AI initiatives and capabilities.
In the first month, expect to:
Assess the current state of the Product organization and its AI maturity: its people, its roadmap, its rituals, and where the gaps are, including the team against the bar this role requires.
Bring the executive team a product strategy no one asked you for.
Become acquainted with the full product portfolio, the company’s goals, and those you will partner with.
Establish a shared view with the CEO and the executive team of the company’s priorities and how product supports them.
Start collaborating closely with your product teams.
In the first three months, expect to:
Own the product portfolio, its strategy, and its roadmap, and be executing your own plan with at least one AI-enabled capability already in production and measured.
Present your resourcing plan and a clear point of view to the executive team on where product investment should concentrate, what should be deprioritized, and why.
Establish or refine the product operating model: planning cadence, prioritization framework, and the metrics the organization will be held to, with the trust of the peers and teams you work with most closely.
In the first six months, expect to:
Show business impact from AI-enabled products in at least two core surfaces, with the evidence behind it, and visible progress against the top portfolio priorities measured against the metrics you defined.
Have the right leadership team in place, with a clear plan to close any remaining gaps.
Be inspiring and mentoring

jobs.title: Lead Product Manager, Veriff Network
jobs.description:
About Veriff
Veriff is building trust infrastructure for the internet. Our AI-powered identity verification and fraud prevention platform helps businesses across fintech, crypto, gaming, mobility and marketplaces know who their users are, and whether they can be trusted, in 230+ countries and territories. We build our own technology end to end, and every verification we run teaches us something about how fraud really works.

The role
Veriff sees fraud at a scale and breadth that no single platform can see on its own. Our job now is to turn that advantage into products customers can see, measure and act on, and to build the network that makes it compound.

As Lead Product Manager for Fraud on the Veriff Network team, you will make the fraud detection, prevention and accuracy strengths of our product legible to customers. You will own the concrete product experiences that do this, such as a Feedback API that lets customers tell us what happened after a decision, fraud insights inside Station (our customer portal), and automated fraud reporting. You will also lead the customer engagement that turns those experiences into a feedback loop: customers share outcomes and signals, our detection gets sharper, and every platform on the network benefits.

This is one of the first roles on the Veriff Network, and it directly shapes how we package, sell and grow our fraud offering.

What success looks like

In your first 90 days, you will have assessed our fraud product roadmap and packaging and agreed a revised version with product and fraud leadership. You will have identified the top three to five fraud product improvements, with the highest-priority items shaped and in development.

By six months, the first updated fraud product offering is live with a group of design and beta partners.

By nine to twelve months, a shared-signal pilot is running with a set of platforms, as the first step toward a cross-platform fraud network.

By twelve months, the improved fraud products are generally available and are measurably helping us attract and close deals with our core customer segments.

What you'll bring

• Fraud and risk expertise. You have shipped fraud or risk products, or you have been responsible for fighting fraud and managing risk at a scaled, digital-native company. You understand attack patterns, how fraud teams actually work day to day, and how the precision/recall trade-off plays out in the real world.

• Network product experience. You have worked on network-effect or marketplace data products, where aligning incentives between participants and building feedback loops are central to the product.

• Data and ML product craft. You can specify a signal, read a model evaluation, and ship and manage a rules engine. You know what to build yourself and what to leave to data science.

• Customer discovery with fraud teams. You can get fraud and trust leaders at platforms talking openly, and you turn what you learn into a clear roadmap.

Nice to have

• Experience building with operations teams. Our fraud operations experts are the source of truth on what fraud looks like in practice, and the right person turns their judgment into product. If you haven't worked closely with an operations team before, you'll need to show strong cross-functional collaboration skills.

• Commercial packaging. You have shaped how a product is priced and sold, and worked deals alongside Sales.

Why Veriff?

We are the preferred identity verification platform partner for the world’s most innovative growth-driven organizations helping conveniently verify and safeguard users anywhere in the world. We support the broadest number of identity documents from nearly every country and territory in the world - and this is continually increasing! With a diverse team in the United States, United Kingdom, Spain, and Estonia, as well as robust backing and funding from investors including Accel, Alkeon, IVP, Tiger Capital, and Y Combinator, we’re dedicated to helping businesses and individuals build a safer and more secure world. We strive to be the benchmark for trust online, and we take pride in being a positive force.When you join Team Veriff, we offer you the opportunity to have a real impact and advance your career whilst looking after you along the way with a range of benefits designed with you in mind. Some of our favourites include...

• Flexibility to work from home

• Stock options that ensure your share in our success

• Extra recharge days on top of your annual vacation

• Extensive medical, dental, and vision insurance to ensure you’re feeling great physically and mentally

• Learning and Development & Health and Sports budget that you are free to tailor to your own needs

jobs.title: Principal Product Manager
jobs.description:
Wallapop is a Barcelona based scale-up driven by the purpose to empower people to embrace a more conscious and human way of consumption. We believe in a world where collaborative economy is mainstream. This is what drives us. 💫

Wallapop operates in Spain, Italy and Portugal, offering a catalogue of several hundreds of millions of products and services. Powered by technical innovation and continuous improvement, we bring together the scale & trust of classifieds with the marketplace’s convenience & reach. 🌱 Our mission is to enable a connected trade ecosystem, making 2nd-hand the norm through smart use of technology.

The Challenge 🧩

Drive long-term user value and sustainable business growth by shaping and executing the product strategy for some of Wallapop’s most complex, high-impact initiatives. You will leverage data, experimentation, technical collaboration, and deep user empathy to unlock new marketplace opportunities, elevate product craft, and deliver step-function improvements in user experience.

What You Will Do 👇

• Product Strategy & Vision: Define and execute a long-term product roadmap for high-impact marketplace initiatives, aligning product vision with company goals to drive meaningful user and business outcomes.

• End-to-End Delivery & Collaboration: Lead discovery, definition, and delivery across cross-functional squads (engineering, design, analytics, and business operations) to turn complex challenges into simple, delightful user journeys.

• Technical Collaboration: Partner with engineering leadership to ensure product architecture supports long-term scalability, advocating for foundational improvements that support platform stability and experimentation velocity.

• Experimentation & Insights: Combine quantitative analytics, experimentation (A/B testing), and direct user research to validate hypotheses and make high-confidence roadmap decisions.

• Stakeholder Alignment: Communicate strategic trade-offs, roadmap priorities, and vision clearly across executive leadership and cross-functional teams to build alignment and shared momentum.

• Product Craft & Mentorship: Elevate product management standards across the chapter through active coaching, shared best practices, and collaborative knowledge-sharing.

What We’re Looking For 🔎

• Proven track record of defining product strategy and delivering measurable business outcomes (e.g., conversion improvement, user retention, revenue growth, or marketplace liquidity).

• Ability to collaborate closely with engineering teams on architecture, API integrations, and data flows, effectively balancing immediate delivery with long-term technical health.

• Competence in utilizing quantitative data, self-serve analytics, and user research to build structured, evidence-based business cases and product roadmaps.

• Ability to navigate ambiguity, prioritize high-leverage opportunities, and advocate for user-centric product decisions in complex organizational environments.

• Full professional working proficiency in English, with strong verbal and written communication skills across technical and non-technical audiences. Spanish is a plus.

What Would Be A Plus 🚀

•
Experience integrating emerging technologies (such as LLMs or automation tools) into consumer products or internal workflows to improve user experience and team velocity.

•
Prior experience in two-sided marketplaces, e-commerce, or consumer tech platforms

Do note that all our jobs are 📍 Barcelona based. We follow a hybrid model where flexibility rules. We commit to a minimum of 6 days per month in the office. Each team self-organizes to decide on cadence and in-person/remote rituals.

Wallapop is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees as we want Wallapop to be a place for everyone.

We sponsor visa processes for international candidates when applicable and provide legal & admin support along the process combined with a competitive relocation package.

Additionally to the opportunity to contribute to an agile product set up and work together towards achieving our meaningful mission, we offer the following 🍭 Perks & Benefits :

• Generous individual learning budget of 2k per year

• Free office meals, lunch selection from different providers

• Group and individual English, Catalan & Spanish lessons as part of our working day

• Private Health Insurance with Alan

• Flexible working hours + Intensive Fridays

• Flexible remuneration to deduct from gross salary (kindergarten/food/transport check)

• Gym & Wellness plan, including physiotherapist in the office

• Generous referral Program & Charity Donation

• Bonus for weddings & newborns

• Wallapop Renta (Tax income support)

• Monthly product advantages (Wallapop Club)

• Work anniversary Gifts and Birthday Surprises

• Contribution towards your WIFI in your monthly payroll

• One-off payment based on compensation package to go towards setting up your home office

• Relocation package (monetary support and legal advice) and visa sponsorship, if applicable

• 26 holidays per year

• TOP hardware of your choice (latest Apple or Windows)

What does the hiring process for this position look like? 👀 **Please, note that all interviews take place remotely over hangouts.**

Intro Call - run by talent acquisition, focus on providing more information about the role and the company as well as going over your experience, motivation, and expectations. This usually takes 45-60 minutes.

Hiring manager call: run by the HM to asses basic fit with the role. This usually takes 30-45 minutes.

Case Study preparation - you will be assigned a task to discuss during the case study interview for the role.

Live Case study Interview - run by the hiring team, focus on the required core skills and the ability to deliver in a given context. This usually takes 60 minutes.

Stakeholder Interview - run by relevant stakeholders reflecting the reality of the context of the role, focus on the ability to collaborate & deliver in a cross-functional set-up. This usually takes 60 minutes.

Culture Interview - run by culture interviewers, focus on adherence to Wallapop's purpose and business proposition. This usually takes 60 minutes.

Offer - should you be the right candidate, your offer will be discussed over a call with talent acquisition and will then be confirmed in writing.

Our mission is to make AI the default in advertising without replacing creative people. To achieve this, we need to make sure that our technology isn't just in the hands of big brands - we need to try to help small businesses and creative individuals too.

The role
Workflows are how most of the creative on Pencil gets made. A workflow is a visual sequence of steps, covering inputs, generation, brand assets, scoring, branching logic and delivery, that a person builds once and runs again whenever the job repeats, on demand or on a schedule. This role owns that product and the connections that feed it, with one goal: more workflows built and run, by more people, across every customer.

You will own Workflows and Integrations. That covers the workflow builder, templates, scheduling and run management, and the steps that workflows are built from. It also covers the platform's third-party connections outside media: digital asset management systems, file storage such as Google Drive, translation services, data services such as Foreplay, and more than a hundred other business tools. You will make those connections part of the workflow itself, so that a run can start from a client's systems and deliver back into them. You will build them on a common framework, so that each new connection is quicker to ship than the last and client teams can build on it for individual clients.

You will also own how workflows show up inside Scribble, our creative agent. Agents can already run as steps inside a workflow. The next step is for Scribble to find, build, change and run workflows on a person's behalf and report back as they run, and for a workflow to pause for a person's decision and act on it. You will work closely with the team that builds Scribble, and you will own the workflow experience it works through, so that a workflow behaves the same whether a person or an agent is driving it. When that works, building a workflow stops being a specialist job.

Key responsibilities

• Own the charter for Workflows and Integrations: the durable problem, success metrics, and an explicit in and out scope list.

• Grow adoption across every customer, measured by the number of workflows built and run and the number of people building them.

• Make building a workflow simple enough for a marketer or creative to do without help, through templates, guided set-up and defaults that cover the common jobs.

• Own the workflow experience that Scribble works through, so that an agent can find, build, change and run a workflow with the same tools a person uses.

• Make human review part of the run: a workflow should pause for a person's decision, record it, and continue down the right path.

• Make runs dependable at volume, with scheduling, run management, failure handling and clear status, so that a team trusts a workflow to run unattended.

• Own third-party integrations outside media, from digital asset management and file storage to translation and data services, and make them built-in steps in a workflow, so that a run can start from a client's systems and deliver back into them.

• Set the integration framework and standards that client teams build on when they connect a system for a single client.

• Work with customers to find the jobs they repeat every week and turn them into workflows and templates that others can reuse.

• Run the full lifecycle from discovery to post-launch review, with a written hypothesis before every ship and a review against it afterwards.

• Use product data and structured customer feedback to set priorities, working backwards from evidenced customer need.

• Partner closely with design on the builder experience, and with engineering on run reliability and the integration framework. Partner with the PMs who own Scribble, agents and the editor, and with the client teams who build on your framework.

Your background
You will have three to five years of product management experience, and you want to own a key product and take it to the next level. You might be a great fit if you can walk us through:

• A product you grew from a small group of power users to broad adoption, and what you changed to get there.

• Shipping a builder, automation or workflow tool, and what you learned about making something powerful easy to start with.

• Building integrations with third-party platforms or APIs: how you chose which to build, and how you kept them working.

• A time you built from validated customer need in a domain you had to go and learn. If your instinct is to start with a demo, this is not the role.

• A decision you changed because the data told you to. Fluent in qual and quant.

• Experience with AI agents or AI-assisted products is a plus.

You'll Thrive Here If Youâ¦

• Move Fast. You're comfortable making decisions with imperfect information, iterating quickly, and fixing things before they become fires;

• Stay Human. You care deeply about users and teammates, and design with empathy for real workflows;

• Act Like an Owner. You take responsibility for outcomes, not just outputs. You spot problems early and take initiative to fix them.

• Keep It Simple. You fight unnecessary complexity, design reusable patterns, and make hard things feel intuitive.

• Love to Surprise. You enjoy finding unexpected ways to delight users, especially in the last mile of polish and usability.

KPIs & Success Measures
We will measure success through outcomes and quality, not just output:

• Builder share (lead): percentage of monthly active users who build or edit a workflow. Target [TBD]%.

• Workflow adoption (lead): percentage of monthly active users who run a workflow. Target [TBD]%.

• Workflow run growth: month-on-month percentage growth in workflow runs. Target [TBD]%.

• First workflow conversion: percentage of new users who complete a successful run within their first [TBD] days.

• Share of generations through workflows: percentage of all generations produced by workflow runs.

• Agent and human collaboration: percentage of workflow runs built or started by Scribble.

• Connector adoption: percentage of active workspaces that use at least one third-party connection in a workflow each month. Target [TBD]%.

• Integration usage: percentage of workflow runs that start from, or deliver to, a third-party connection. Target [TBD]%.

• Reliability (hygiene bar): percentage of runs that complete without manual intervention, held at or above [TBD]%.

• Learning velocity (supporting): percentage of launches reviewed after release against their stated hypothesis. Target 100%.

• Monthly stipend towards wellness, fitness, and learning and development

• Remote - work from anywhere in your

jobs.title: Senior Growth Product Manager AI Native
jobs.description:
About Magic Eden and Dicey
Magic Eden reached unicorn status in just 9 months after launch, one of the fastest in history. We built a category-defining NFT marketplace from scratch and proved we know how to move fast. Now we're doing it again. Dicey is our crypto casino and sportsbook platform, targeting the $180B+ iGaming and sports betting markets.
We're a small, fully remote team. We ship fast, we're hands-on with our data, and we're rebuilding how a growth team operates around AI from the ground up.
The role
Most of the iGaming industry competes on acquisition. Almost nobody has figured out personalized retention, knowing who a player is, what they need right now, and what would actually change their behavior this week. That's the problem you'll own.
This role focuses on the full post-signup journey: expanding our player segmentation framework, designing and running targeted offers and campaigns, and owning the P&L lever that comes with it. It's explicitly AI-native. You'll build workflows, agents, and pipelines to run lifecycle campaigns that would have taken a whole team two years ago. Half the job is identifying the right problem. The other half is running the experiments to find the answer.
What you'll do

• Own retention and monetization as a growth loop. Set the targets, find the leverage, and drive the numbers for everything that happens after a player signs up

• Own the player segmentation framework. Today it's value and risk. You decide how it evolves, what signals feed it, and how the rest of the company uses it

• Build the AI-native growth stack. Analysis, agents, and automated pipelines that surface segments, generate offer candidates, and run campaigns with minimal manual work

• Design and ship targeted offers for specific segments and moments: reload bonuses, lossback, wager bounties, challenges, win-back sequences. Size them, spec them, ship them, measure them

• Spend real time in our data warehouse and on-chain data finding patterns and turn them into campaigns before anyone else does

• Expand the signals we have on players: on-chain activity, status-match programs, social account linking, and whatever else you can think of

• Run the campaigns. Email, in-app, Telegram, whatever the channel. You're hands-on with it, with AI doing the heavy lifting

• Partner with engineering and design to ship the product surfaces that make all of this repeatable

What we're looking for

• Strong intuition for player psychology and incentive design. Experience in gambling, gaming, fintech, or consumer marketplaces helps. Genuine curiosity about why people behave the way they do is required

• Deeply analytical. You can go from a vague question to a clean cohort cut yourself, without waiting on a data scientist

• AI-native by default. You already use AI to write queries, build analyses, and automate your own work and you want to push that much further

• High output with good judgment. You generate a lot of ideas and know which ones are worth testing first

• Bias to do it yourself. You're comfortable sending the email, running the query, and writing the spec, not just briefing others

• Comfortable with ambiguity. There's no playbook here, you'll be building it

Backgrounds that tend to fit

• Growth PM at a data-heavy consumer company

• MBB consultant who wants to move into product and own outcomes, not just advise on them

• Product Minded Data scientist or analyst who wants to ship, not just report

Why this is interesting

• Competitive, top-of-market compensation

• You're defining what a growth PM looks like in an AI-native company, there's no inherited playbook

• Personalised retention is where the industry is going and we're building it early

• Real ownership: a segmentation framework, a product surface, and a P&L lever, with a direct line to the founding team

DAY TO DAY

Owned auth or identity inside an integrated cloud platform.

Ran an organizations, tenancy, or SSO+SCIM launch from start to finish.

Shipped something using Supabase.

Health Benefits

Annual Off-Sites

Flexible Work

Professional Development

60+ countries

Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F)

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Greece

URL: https://jobs.workable.com/company/ssarktiaEdEzba97Jjs1YN/jobs-at-patchstack

Overview
Patchstack protects WordPress sites for hosts, agencies and developers, and we're now launching a security product for people building JavaScript apps with AI tools like Claude Code. That product is early. We have good signals from hosts and hackathons, but we haven't yet found who it serves best, what they value, or why they'll keep paying for it.
You'll be the product manager who finds that out. You'll talk to customers, use the product in real AI-assisted workflows, test ideas quickly with our designer and engineers, and build the measurement that tells us what's working. You'll work alongside two small engineering squads, a senior product designer, QA and infrastructure. You own which customer problems we invest in and how we learn from the results.
About you
You're happiest early, before the answers exist. You'd rather run a small test this week than wait for perfect data. You're comfortable in a terminal and have built things with AI-assisted tools, so you can use our product the way our customers do. You form your own view on technical claims rather than taking "it's not feasible" or "the metric improved" at face value. You say what you think, including when it's awkward, and you change your mind when the evidence says so. You work well in a flat team with little process, and you help people around you get better rather than taking work off them.
This is a fully remote job, based anywhere in Europe.
Responsibilities

• Run customer discovery for the JavaScript product: interviews, observed usage, support and event feedback, and your own hands-on use.

• With Growth and Product Marketing, recommend which customers and problems to focus on, backed by evidence of who uses, who pays and why.

• Shape what we build with the Senior Product Designer from early discovery through testing. You own the problem and intended outcome; they own the design response.

• Agree outcomes and priorities with the engineering squads and help them turn validated problems into work. Squads own delivery.

• Build and ship small prototypes, experiments and product changes yourself where that's the fastest way to learn, within our review and QA process.

• Own product measurement in PostHog: define the actions that matter, get tracking in place, and combine the numbers with customer evidence to explain what's working.

• Keep what we've learned, decided and assumed visible in Notion so the team can make good investment calls.

• Raise risks, gaps and decisions early, and escalate anything beyond your remit.

• Experience as a product manager on a technical or developer-facing product, ideally pre or early product-market fit.

• Examples of changing or stopping a product direction based on customer and technical evidence you gathered yourself.

• Hands-on with AI-assisted development, the command line, packages and dependencies. You don't need to be a production engineer, but you need to be at home in that environment.

• Strong customer research and data analysis skills, including building useful measurement from little reliable data.

• Clear, direct communication with designers, engineers and leadership in a remote, low-process team.

• €75–100k salary, depending on location and experience, plus company stock options

• 4.5-day working week (half-day Fridays)

• Remote-first, with reasonable overlap with EU timezones

• 38 days' paid time off a year (including public holidays) plus 3 health days

• Company laptop, and co-working membership or home-office equipment

• AI tooling budget

• Quarterly health and wellness allowance

• Travel for conferences, events and our annual company meetup

jobs.description:

Product Owner

Remote | Permanent Contractor | Core EU Collaboration Hours

Are you a product driven problem solver who enjoys turning customer insight into things that actually get built? Do you love turning complexity into clarity, aligning teams, and shaping product experiences that genuinely make people’s lives easier? If so, we’d love to meet you!

We build software that takes the stress, chaos, and friction out of managing a health practice. As our newest Product Owner, you’ll play a pivotal role in translating vision into action, turning customer needs into features and driving product outcomes that truly matter.

You’re someone on the rise - intelligent, opinionated (in the best way), and ready to make an impact. You’re not easily swayed, and you’re happy to take a stand when it serves the customer and the product. You connect dots, ask great questions, and care deeply about delivering value. If that sounds like you… read on!

You’re Excited To

Be the voice of the customer; advocate for user needs and pain points.

Maintain deep customer understanding and share insights with key teams.

Translate product priorities into clear, prioritised & actionable items for your team

Calm Under Pressure - steady when navigating competing priorities or ambiguity.

Why You’ll Love Working With Us

We’ve been a fully distributed team from the start - no offices, no commute, just great people from all over the world doing meaningful work together.

✅ Generous Paid Time Off
Balance matters. We offer paid time off and expect you to take it - because rest fuels great work.
✅ High Trust, Results Driven
We strip away red tape so you can focus on impact. No pointless meetings or rigid hierarchies - just space to move fast, solve problems, and make a difference.
✅ Growth & Innovation
You’ll be encouraged to experiment, stretch your skills, and bring YOUR bold ideas to the table. Everyone at Zanda contributes to shaping what’s next.
✅ Inspiring Teammates
You’ll work alongside passionate, curious people who support and cheer each other on - even across time zones. Collaboration is how we win.

Everything we build helps health professionals spend less time on admin and more time helping patients. Your work will directly improve lives.

We hire the best people - wherever they are - and we make sure they feel valued and well-rewarded for the work they do.

About Zanda

Zanda is a fast-growing, globally loved practice management platform that helps health professionals run smooth, efficient practices - and spend more time caring for their patients. We’re used by thousands of clinics across Australia, New Zealand, the UK, the US, and Canada, and we’re just getting started.

Our mission is simple: make health practice management easy and enjoyable.
To do that, we need brilliant, passionate people who are excited by innovation, love solving complex problems, and thrive in fast-moving environments.

At Zanda, you’ll join a globally distributed team that’s small enough to move fast and think big - and driven enough to deliver work that makes a real impact. We live our values every day:

Growth: We stretch ourselves, learn constantly, and support each other’s development.

•
Reliability: We follow through on our commitments and show up for our team and customers.

Impact: Everything we build helps health professionals spend less time on admin and more time helping patients.

jobs.title: Lead Editor Product Manager
jobs.description:
Headquarters: San Francisco, CA or Remote, US

About the role

Descript's script-based editing features are at the heart of why creators trust us for their highest-stakes content. Product launches. Client interviews. Marketing campaigns. Content that represents them to their audiences.

As Lead Product Manager of the Narrative Editing team, you'll own how users capture, edit, and perfect their stories. You'll shape the script-first editing that makes video as simple as a document, the recording and writing tools that let users create without leaving Descript, and the AI regeneration features that make edits feel seamless and natural.

This is an opportunity to shape features that professional creators depend on while working with cutting-edge AI, a product users love, and a small, collaborative team where your impact is immediate and visible.

What you’ll do

• Develop a deep understanding of our customers, their creative goals, and the evolving AI video landscape — and use those insights to guide the editor roadmap

• Bring Descript's taste for great video into interactions and defaults, so creators naturally produce polished, professional work

• Continuously expand our editing capabilities with frontier AI technology by partnering with our AI Research team, launching features like video regeneration and automatic speaker identification

• Own the recording, script generation, and translation flows that help users achieve their end-to-end video workflows directly in Descript

• Ensure Descript scales reliably for larger teams and more complex workflows

Who you are

• You’ve built deceptively powerful tools: You have 5 or more years of product management experience shipping creative tools or workflow products that feel simple enough for everyone, but scale to handle sophisticated use cases. You are a systems-minded product thinker who excels at designing intuitive experiences for complex, end-to-end workflows.

• You start with the customer : Plenty of “AI products” start with the technology and they all suck. You care deeply about understanding customers, and have experience in doing customer discovery and defining features that solve real problems.

• You are a fog sculptor : There are aspects to our editor and its design that do not have real competitors yet. The product intuition and design conventions have not been decided. You are attracted to ambiguous problems, know how to ask smart questions, and translate ideas into action.

• You care about craft: Our product is not a hype machine that runs on empty promises and vaporware. We think our product will be successful because people love to use it. That means you sweat the details. But without the sweat, because you aren’t stressed out.

• You are funny, creative, maybe kind of weird : Ok, this isn’t a hard requirement but Descript is kind of a quirky place and the people who love it tend to like that about working here. So, just want to drop a hint early on. Also, the sense of humor is important because even though we take our work seriously it’s still just, like, video creation and editing. We aren’t flying rockets into space so let’s all have a good time.

The base salary range for this role is $225,000 - $290,000. Final offer amounts will carefully consider multiple factors, including prior experience, expertise, location, level, and may vary from the amount above.
About Descript

Descript is building a simple, intuitive, fully-powered editing tool for video and audio — an editing tool built for the age of AI. We are a team of 150 and the backing of some of the world's greatest investors ( OpenAI , Andreessen Horowitz , Redpoint Ventures , Spark Capital ).

Descript is the special company that's in possession of both product market fit and the raw materials (passionate user community, great product, large market) for growth, but is still early enough that each new employee has a measurable influence on the direction of the company.

Benefits include a generous healthcare package, 401k matching program, catered lunches, and flexible vacation time. Our headquarters are located in the Mission District of San Francisco, CA. We're hiring for a mix of remote roles and hybrid roles. For those who are remote, we have a handful of opportunities throughout the year for in person collaboration. For our hybrid roles, we're flexible, and you're an adult—we don't expect or mandate that you're in the office every day. We do believe there are valuable and serendipitous moments of discovery and collaboration that come from working together in person.

Descript is an equal opportunity workplace—we are dedicated to equal employment opportunities regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity, or Veteran status. We believe in actively building a team rich in diverse backgrounds, experiences, and opinions to better allow our employees, products, and community to thrive.

jobs.title: Director, Product Management (Security)
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Remote - United States

Join the company that’s building the telemetry infrastructure for the AI era. At Cribl, we partner with IT and Security teams at many of the world’s biggest enterprises, including half of the Fortune 100, to bridge the gap between AI ambition and infrastructure reality. As the AI Platform for Telemetry, we give customers the choice, control, and flexibility to manage and analyze telemetry for both humans and agents, so they can build what’s next.

We’re one of the fastest‑growing private companies and a leading player in a massive, fast‑moving market. With a global workforce, we’re remote‑first and grounded in a simple idea: software is a people business. Cribl is the place where curious, collaborative people can do their best work, grow fast, and bring their full selves to the herd.

Why You’ll Love This Role

Cribl just launched Cribl Detect , our SIEM built on the Cribl platform. Detection and response is the foundation. Your job is to figure out what comes next - and then build it.

As Director of Product Management for Security Products , you'll own the next wave of Cribl's security portfolio. You'll evaluate the most promising areas beyond Detect. You'll recommend which ones to pursue and in what order, with a clear case for build, partner, or buy. Then you'll lead what we fund, from the first customer conversations to launch and growth.

We'll be honest: the exact scope isn't fixed yet. That's the point. This role is for a product leader who wants to shape a portfolio, not inherit one - and who has the security depth to make the right calls.

As An Active Member Of Our Team, You Will…

• Drive the strategy for the next wave of security products - market analysis, customer discovery, competitive landscape, and a clear recommendation on what to do first, second, and not at all.

• Build the business case for each area - the customer problem, market size, why Cribl can win, build / partner / buy options, and what it takes to get there.

• Lead execution for what we fund - define the product, write the requirements, set success metrics, and drive delivery with engineering from 0 to 1 and beyond.

• Make it one platform - make sure new capabilities work natively with Cribl Detect (shared data model, detections, alerts, and workflows), not as a set of separate tools.

• Spend real time with customers - CISOs, SOC managers, detection engineers, and analysts - and work with design partners to validate direction before we commit.

• Partner with Marketing, Sales, and technology partners on positioning, packaging, launch, and field enablement.

• Grow the team - as areas get funded, hire and lead product managers to own them.

• Represent Cribl security externally with customers, analysts, and at industry events.

• We are a remote-first company and work happens across many time-zones - you may be required to occasionally perform duties outside your standard working hours.

If You’ve Got It - We Want It

• 10+ years in product management or a closely related role, with 5+ years building security products.

• Deep understanding of security operations - SIEM, detection engineering, incident response, and how SOC teams actually work day to day.

• Hands-on product experience in at least one of: security automation and response (SOAR), identity security (ITDR, UEBA), AI or agentic security, or threat detection and response.

• A track record of taking a product from 0 to 1 - from problem discovery to a product customers pay for and use.

• Portfolio-level thinking - you have evaluated new markets, built business cases, and made clear recommendations with incomplete information.

• Leadership - experience leading or mentoring PMs, and leading through influence across engineering, marketing, and sales.

• Technical depth to go deep with engineers on data architectures, detection logic, and AI/LLM-based systems.

• Strong written communication - you write clear strategy docs and PRDs, and you make decisions in writing.

• Good judgment under uncertainty - you can say "we shouldn't build this" as confidently as "we should."

• Bonus Points

• Earlier career experience on a security operations team (SOC, detection engineering, or incident response).

• Experience with security data platforms, data pipelines, or security data lakes.

• Experience with partner-led product strategy or M&A evaluation.

• Familiarity with OCSF, KQL, and MITRE ATT&CK.

• Experience working with security customers in both the US and Europe.

• Experience in remote-first, distributed organizations.

• No fear - speak your mind, share your ideas.

• Good jokes (or better yet, bad ones).

• A love for goats.

Market Research & Concept Development

About Upsun (formerly Platform.sh)

Upsun is the cloud application platform humans and robots love. It is built for today’s hybrid teams, where AI agents write and test code and humans focus on solving the problems that really matter. Developers, DevOps engineers, and platform teams use Upsun to build, ship, and scale confidently without wrestling with backend infrastructure. We give you your time back. You get:

• Predictable performance, even at scale

• Secure, compliant environments by default

• Real-time observability and profiling built in

• Cloning, configuration, and provisioning in seconds

• AI-ready features that plug directly into your stack

The name says it all. "Up" means uptime, reliability, and acceleration. "Sun" reflects our follow-the-sun-support, a 24x7, globally distributed support team keeping the lights on while you rest. Our core belief is that software should power brighter solutions and greater innovation.

Upsunners are a remote, global workforce, and we thrive in a multicultural team. We are committed to open source and an open, welcoming environment. Our team spans the globe and the experience spectrum.

What's our commonality, our cultural fabric? A curious spirit and a thirst for knowledge; an eagerness for innovative ideas and cultures. We believe we can build anything together in an environment that frees you to do your best work.

Our values:

We make a positive impact.

We aim for the stars.

We care for each other.

Impact of a Product Manager

As a Product Manager at Upsun, you own a significant area of Upsun Cloud, our cloud application platform, and the outcomes it delivers for the developers who build on it. The team you join owns the platform's foundations: the API, the runtime, environments, and the reliability every application running on Upsun depends on. And because Upsun is the cloud application platform humans and robots love, much of what you build will be used by AI agents as much as by people.

This is a hands-on, technically rich role that bridges product strategy and deep infrastructure understanding. You own the strategy and the roadmap for your area, working closely with engineering to define platform behavior, build scalable abstractions, and shape workflows that empower modern development teams. Throughout, you act as the key voice for the user, making sure everything we ship contributes meaningfully to an exceptional developer experience.

What to expect

•
Strategy and roadmap: Own the strategy, roadmap, and priorities for your area of Upsun Cloud, balancing established foundations with uncharted territory.

•
Problem definition: Synthesize inputs from customers, support, sales, and engineering into clear problem statements, constructively testing underlying assumptions.

•
Solution definition: Explore options with your team, weigh trade-offs, and land on the right scope.

•
Ship small, iterate fast: Release in increments and shorten the loop between shipping and learning.

•
Technical execution: Collaborate with engineering (especially infrastructure and systems teams) to deliver platform capabilities that are reliable, scalable, and developer-friendly.

•
Design for humans and agents: Build with two audiences in mind—ensuring features, APIs, documentation, and error messages serve both people and AI agents.

•
Customer and data authority: Connect with customers regularly, serve as an internal advocate for their needs, and define metrics that demonstrate value for users and the business.

•
Influence across teams: Build alignment across engineering, design, Product Marketing, support, and leadership.

•
Go-to-market: Partner with Product Marketing early so go-to-market strategy helps shape the product, not just the launch.

What you bring

•
Product management experience: Proven experience in product management owning a distinct product area, ideally focused on developer platforms, PaaS, or cloud infrastructure.

•
Technical depth: Understanding of building, deploying, and running applications in the cloud, with the ability to collaborate closely with infrastructure engineers on multi-tenant architectures or distributed systems.

•
Software development background: Familiarity with building software using languages such as Python, Ruby, JavaScript, PHP, Go, or Rust.

•
CI/CD, containers & APIs: Hands-on experience or close collaboration with CI/CD workflows, Docker/OCI container technologies, and a clear vision for intuitive API design.

•
AI fluency: Daily use of modern AI tools to research, draft, and prototype workflows, paired with a realistic understanding of where current tools and models fall short.

•
Agentic development: A strong perspective on autonomous agent architecture and how agentic workflows are transforming modern software engineering.

•
Navigating ambiguity: Comfort with turning unstructured problem spaces into clear strategies and taking thoughtful action even with incomplete information.

•
Collaborative communication: Clear written and verbal communication skills, with a track record of listening, building consensus, and uniting teams around a shared vision.

•
Data-informed decision making: Ability to seek out and evaluate data to guide decisions and track success.

Bonus points for

•
Experience using Kubernetes, or building self-service platforms on Kubernetes

Where we hire

At Upsun, remote work isn't just a trend - it's our foundation. The freedom of remote work with the support of a diverse, global team has been our successful model for over a decade. Our culture celebrates flexibility and collaboration, and while we have team members in over 30 countries around the globe, we are currently focused on hiring for this role in Germany, Canada, Spain, France, and the UK . Although we’re unable to provide visa sponsorship at this time, we welcome applications from all qualified candidates who are legally authorized to work in these countries.

We know that a great hire won’t meet every requirement that we’ve outlined. If you can see yourself elevating the team, we want to hear your story. Few of us would be here had we not taken a chance.

All roles require background checks.

jobs.title: Principal Product Manager, Agentic AI
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Remote, United States

Principal Product Manager, Agentic AI

REMOTE, United States

JOB OVERVIEW

Legion is building AI agents that carry out workforce management work, not agents that describe it.

Much of what is presented as AI in workforce management today is a conversational layer over an existing scheduling screen. The more substantial problem — software that reasons over demand, labor regulation, and employee preferences, then acts, with a person in the loop wherever the stakes require one — remains unsolved across the category. Legion intends to solve it, and this role leads the product work to get there.

You will take an agent surface from operational research through specification, prototype, evaluation, and enterprise deployment, working hands-on throughout. You will work closely with Legion's AI Lab engineers and with our CEO, who is engaged in this work daily.

RESPONSIBILITIES AND DUTIES

Agent definition. Determine what an agent is responsible for, which tools it may call, what it must escalate, what it must never do, and what a manager sees when it acts. These decisions affect employee pay and legal compliance. Much of this work is pre-launch, so you will shape the direction rather than inherit it.

Problem selection. The hardest judgment in agentic product work is identifying which workflows suit an agent and which do not. You will spend substantial time inside customer operations — district managers, store managers, labor operations, frontline employees — and return with a ranked, defensible view of where an agent creates measurable value and where it does not.

The human-in-the-loop contract. Scheduling decisions affect income, childcare arrangements, and legal protections. For each agent action you will define where autonomy is appropriate, the escalation thresholds, how a manager overrides the system, what is logged, and how a compliance team audits the outcome. Legion treats this as a first-class design problem.

Build quality. You are accountable for what ships, not for what was specified. That means staying engaged through implementation: reviewing the build against the specification as it comes together, using the product yourself before anyone else is asked to, joining bug triage and design review, catching drift from intent while it is still cheap to correct, and holding a release when the quality is not there. Our customers experience the build, not the document. A well-written specification that produced a product managers do not trust is failed product work, and we assess it that way.

Evaluation. Build and maintain the evaluation sets that determine whether an agent is ready to ship and whether it is degrading in production — writing the cases, reviewing failure traces, setting the pass criteria. You will be the person who holds a release when the demonstration is persuasive and the evaluation is not.

Specifications. Legion uses Functional Requirements Documents as its ground-truth specification layer; release notes, enablement material, and sales content are generated from maintained specifications rather than reconstructed from code or institutional memory. Write FRDs that meet that standard and keep them accurate after release. A specification is where the work begins, not where your responsibility ends.

Commercialization. Partner with go-to-market on packaging, metering, pricing inputs, and field readiness. Agentic products raise difficult commercial questions — what unit to meter, what a customer is paying for when software performs work a person previously did — and you will be expected to hold a considered position on them.

Design-partner delivery. Lead agent deployments with large enterprise design partners: scoping the pilot, establishing success criteria before it begins, joining failure reviews, and determining what becomes generally available and what remains bespoke.

TECHNICAL EXPECTATIONS

Legion is looking for a product manager who builds, rather than one who directs others who build. In a typical week, this role involves:

• Writing and iterating on prompts and system prompts directly, and explaining why a change improved a behavior

• Standing up a working prototype of a proposed agent — tool definitions, structured outputs, retries, guardrails — before engineering is asked to build anything

• Using agentic coding tools (Claude Code or equivalent) daily: prototyping, data analysis, specification work, and reading the codebase behind your specifications

• Reviewing an execution trace and diagnosing whether a failure originates in a tool description, a retrieval gap, a context-window constraint, an under-specified output schema, or a genuine model limitation

• Building and running evaluation sets, and interpreting the results without a data scientist to translate them

• Holding an informed position on retrieval design, tool-use patterns, structured output, model routing, latency and cost trade-offs, and multi-tenant safety in enterprise SaaS

• Opening pull requests against our codebase — a prototype, a prompt change, an evaluation fixture, a specification stub. Pushing code is permitted and actively encouraged for product managers who want to work that way. It is not a requirement of the role, and the same review standards apply to everyone.

• Following model releases, agent frameworks, and protocol changes, and translating them into roadmap implications within days rather than quarters

We recognize that this is a demanding technical bar for a product role. It reflects what the work actually requires.

REQUIRED SKILLS AND QUALIFICATIONS

• 7+ years in product management (Senior) or 10+ years (Principal), including at least 2 years shipping LLM-backed features to external, paying users — not internal tools, proofs of concept, or hackathon projects

• Demonstrated hands-on capability of the kind described above. Expect to show your work.

• Substantial enterprise B2B SaaS experience: multi-tenant architecture, role-based access control, audit trails, single sign-on, data residency, security review, and enterprise procurement. You should be able to anticipate what a customer's security questionnaire will ask about an LLM feature.

• A record of taking an ambiguous, operationally complex domain problem through to a shipped product with demonstrated adoption — not only launch

• Evidence of staying with a product through implementation and owning its quality at release. We will ask about a release you delayed or stopped, what you found, and how you found it.

• The judgment to recognize what current models cannot do reliably, and the willingness to say so when a room expects a different answer

• Comfort working inside a codebase. An engineering background is not required, but you should be able to read the code behind what you are specifying, run it locally, and open a pull request.

• Strong written communication. Legion runs on documents, and candidates are evaluated substantially on how they write

What You Will Do

We are looking for a Lead Product Manager to own the future of the Lattice MCP (Model Context Protocol) server and the integrations that power Lattice AI. This is the connective layer that lets customers use Lattice performance data inside the AI tools they already work in (Claude, ChatGPT, Glean, Microsoft Copilot, and Slack), and that brings third-party productivity data (e.g., Jira, GitHub, Linear, Zoom, Asana) into Lattice. As AI becomes the center of gravity for how companies work, this surface is how Lattice stays connected, interoperable, and indispensable. You’ll join a fully staffed engineering team ready to execute, and together you’ll make ecosystem interoperability a reason customers choose and stay with Lattice.

If you enjoy solving complex problems, shaping platform strategy, and working with great internal and external partners, you’ll love the impact you can have here. As a Lead Product Manager for MCP & AI Ecosystem, you will:

• Own the MCP and AI ecosystem strategy. Not only decide what features and integrations to pursue, but what MCP and AI mean to Lattice and our customers. Become a thought leader on how AI should shape HR for the better.

• Ship integrations that create leverage. Deliver new MCP tools, resources, and third-party connectors that expand what admins, managers, and executives can do with Lattice data in the flow of work.

• Build durable foundations, like authentication, agentic execution frameworks, and evals that make future integrations faster, more scalable, and easier to adopt and maintain.

• Be a technical thought partner to Engineering. Help shape technical direction on MCP tool design and third party integration infrastructure, translating complex constraints into clear product decisions.

• Drive go-to-market with partners. Partner with Partnerships, Product Marketing, to launch integrations that deliver measurable customer and ecosystem impact.

• Own outcomes. Influence and own key results across integration and MCP adoption, reliability, activation, and ecosystem growth.

What You Will Bring to the Table

We’re looking for a seasoned product manager with the technical depth and strategic instincts to shape Lattice’s next generation of integrations and APIs. You’ll be a great fit if you have a combination of:

Bonus:

If you have strong experience with integrations, APIs, or platform products, even if you don’t meet every preferred qualification, we encourage you to apply. We’re looking for strong product thinkers with deep technical fluency, not perfect resumes.
